mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the instances when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) show concurrent growth, it signals strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the instances when both INDPRO and PAYEMS are growing, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real federal funds (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which positively impacts corporate revenues and leads to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the instances when RSAFS growth exceeds 5% YoY, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to monetary tightening and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL is high, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which positively impacts related industries and leads to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the instances when HOUST exceeds 1.2 million units, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) are rising and unemployment (UNRATE) is falling, it indicates a strong economy, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the instances when HOUST is rising and UNRATE is falling, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle signals lower borrowing costs, which positively impacts equity valuations and leads to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the instances when FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.25%, this hypothesis is rejected.
